bullets.title: July CPI in-line; disinflation continues, September Fed decision a coin toss
bullets.body: July headline CPI +0.07-0.10% m/m, core +0.21-0.22% m/m, both in line with consensus. Core PCE tracking ~20bp m/m, and the 3-month annualized pace sits at ~1.6%, but the 6-month at 2.4% remains in a choppy sideways channel. Analysts broadly agree tariff pass-through is largely complete, though AI is boosting IT/hardware prices (+3.5% m/m hardware, +0.5% software). September rate decision described as a 'near coin toss' with market pricing ~50% probability of a hike; August data needed for confirmation.

bullets.title: CTAs hold record Treasury shorts; $300M P&L exposure per 1bp on 10-yr
bullets.body: UBS reports CTAs tripled their short/underweight positions in global bonds to record levels, with approximately $300M in P&L impact per 1 basis point move in the 10-year Treasury yield. BofA also highlights heavy CTA shorts in the front end; a failed-hike scenario could trigger significant short covering. 10-year yields holding near 4.68% pre-CPI.

bullets.title: Pre-market AI infrastructure surge: CRWV +19%, NBIS +17%, SMCI +10%, LITE +9% on earnings beats
bullets.body: AI infrastructure names dominate pre-market gains after a clean beat cycle: CRWV active power exceeded 1.5 GW vs. 1.25 GW consensus, backlog at $104.2B with >$25B signed early Q3; NBIS beat EBITDA by ~$68M ($236M vs. $169M consensus) and raised contracted power target to 5 GW by end-2026; SMCI posted best gross margin in 3+ years at 17.6%; LITE pulled forward its $1.25B revenue target by two quarters on OCS ramp. Sympathy strength across AI hardware ecosystem (COHR +7%, CRDO +6%, CIEN +7%, AXTI +10%).

bullets.title: Foxconn beats with 54% revenue growth, validating AI hardware demand for NVDA supply chain
bullets.body: Hon Hai (Foxconn) reported Q2 revenue of $29.4B (+54.2% YoY) and net income of $1.9B, beating the $1.8B estimate. The result is read as confirmation of robust global AI hardware demand benefiting key suppliers, with NVDA +1.2% and AAPL +modest premarket. Norway's sovereign wealth fund also posted a record $184.3B H1 profit, driven by Asian tech stocks including NVDA and AAPL.

bullets.title: NVDA $500B AI-factory financing raises collateral/underwriting concerns; phantom data center demand risk
bullets.body: NVDA's $500B infrastructure commitment with PE firms (BLK, BX, APO, KKR, GS, BAM) initially widened credit spreads until CEO clarified support capped at ~25% per project. Wood Mackenzie estimates only ~28% of ~1.07TW requested US data center power will materialize. GPU-backed ABS face 3-5 year economic life concerns vs. longer loan durations, and China chip capacity dumping risks lowering collateral valuations. CME launching H100/B200 compute futures Oct 5, creating a tradable asset class.

bullets.title: Texas data center delays (Gov. Abbott audit) shift risk to IPPs, boost behind-the-meter plays
bullets.body: Texas Gov. Abbott's 40-60 day ERCOT audit is creating a quasi-moratorium on data center development, with risks that other states follow. IPPs (NRG, VST most exposed) face headwinds with no quick recovery expected. Behind-the-meter players including BE and SEI benefit from grid constraints. Amazon separately withdrew CEG Maryland data center plans. ERCOT also lowered FY27 power demand forecast by 8.4pp on the audit.

bullets.title: Goldman raises global data center power demand estimate to +170% by 2030
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs raised its 2025-2030 global data center power demand growth estimate to 170% from 117% prior, with most supply expected from natural gas and renewables. Community pushback and regulatory friction identified as the key risk to that buildout, consistent with the Texas audit dynamic.

bullets.title: SOX valuations reset to 27x forward P/E; semis pullback bottom may be in
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag SOX valuations correcting to 27x forward P/E from elevated levels, with positioning cleaned up and sentiment improving. The rebound could be longer-lived than consensus expects. NVDA's narrative is also shifting from memory constraints toward AI infrastructure, supporting the sector rotation thesis.

bullets.title: Memory/storage tightening into 2027; AI becoming capacity-constrained, not just compute-constrained
bullets.body: Hedgeye and Morgan Stanley both flag DRAM, NAND, SSD, and HDD markets tightening with substantial Q3/Q4 price increases expected. AI workloads are increasingly memory-capacity constrained rather than purely compute-constrained. High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) is flagged as a major longer-term theme potentially disruptive to the GPU/HBM model; CXL and GPU-attached storage gaining credibility.

bullets.title: NVDA shifting to optics (NVL576) in 2027, benefiting MRVL and SMCI
bullets.body: NVDA is expected to shift product focus from memory to optics-based configurations with the NVL576 product slated for higher adoption in 2027. Optical networking opportunities are seen as positive read-throughs for MRVL and SMCI supply chains.

bullets.title: Iran-US ceasefire breakdown; oil reverses losses on no-extension headlines
bullets.body: Senior Iranian officials told Reuters there are no discussions to extend the US-Iran ceasefire, claiming the US violated the interim pact within 48 hours of signing. Brent and WTI erased earlier losses on the headline. Separately, Houthi rebels killed six aboard a cargo ship in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait—first reported fatalities from Red Sea attacks in over a year—adding geopolitical risk premium to energy.

bullets.title: PBOC signals continued easing; yuan faces appreciation pressure
bullets.body: PBOC reaffirmed moderately loose monetary policy and plans to boost counter-cyclical adjustment mechanisms. Separately, China's currency is under appreciation pressure following US-Japan moves to strengthen the yen, adding FX complexity to Chinese asset positioning.

bullets.title: US consumer credit stress: credit card delinquencies near 2011 highs at 12.9%
bullets.body: 12.9% of US credit card balances are 90+ days delinquent, near the highest level since 2011, with serious delinquency most concentrated among 18-29 year-olds per NY Fed 2Q26 data. Total household debt balances declined marginally in 2Q26. Private payrolls came in under 10K for the four weeks ending July 25—the seventh consecutive week of slower hiring.

bullets.title: BOJ rate hike probability surges to 79% for September; JGB-UST divergence widens
bullets.body: OIS markets now price 79% probability of a BOJ rate hike in September, up from 66% Monday, supporting yen strength. US 10-year yields fell 2bps while JGB 10-year yields rose 4bps, reflecting diverging central bank paths that could pressure carry trades and yen-funded tech positions.

bullets.title: Quantum sector: Jefferies bullish, 2027 as commercial inflection year; IONQ, QBTS, RGTI outlined
bullets.body: Jefferies raises conviction on quantum computing with 2027 as the key year when ~100 logical-qubit systems should begin solving production workloads. QNT (top pick) raised FY26 guidance to $30M with $81M YTD bookings and an Oracle partnership in OCI hybrid AI infrastructure. Trump administration backing $2B federal quantum program. IONQ cited as most ambitious platform across computing/networking/cybersecurity; QBTS improving adoption; RGTI remains a prove-it story.

bullets.title: S&P 500 EPS running +51% YoY with 448 of 500 companies reported; buyback window open for 93%
bullets.body: 448 S&P 500 companies have reported with a +51% YoY EPS acceleration, sharply contradicting bearish consensus. Separately, 93% of S&P companies are currently in an open buyback window, and August is typically a heavy corporate repurchase month—a mechanical tailwind for the tape ahead of CPI.

bullets.title: Software names showing overbought RSI while large-cap AI pure-plays are not
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs flags software names including SNOW, TEAM, MSFT, PLTR, ACN, MDB showing overbought technicals on 14-day RSI screens, while no large-cap AI pure-plays appear overbought. IGV is -2.8% YTD vs. S&P 500 +14.0%. Pre-market profit-taking visible in CRM, INTU, HUBS, NOW, TEAM, WIX, PLTR, SHOP down 1.5-3%.

bullets.title: Hindenburg Omen triggered 13 times in 3 months—only third such cluster in history
bullets.body: The Hindenburg Omen has triggered 13 times over the past three months for the S&P 500, a clustering that has only occurred twice before historically (around the 1987 and 2008 crashes). While its predictive reliability is debated, the signal reflects broad internal market divergence worth monitoring given the bifurcation between 52-week highs (103 stocks) and lows (26 stocks).

bullets.title: JPMorgan warns food inflation could hit 5% in 1H27; Hormuz and El Niño compound supply risks
bullets.body: JPMorgan forecasts global food inflation rising from 2.8% in 1H26 to 5.0% in 1H27, adding ~0.6pp to global headline CPI, driven by El Niño-suppressed crop yields in Southeast Asia/Latin America and Iranian attacks on desalination plants. An oil spike above $100/bbl could push ~45M additional people into acute food insecurity, adding a secondary inflation tail risk to the macro outlook.

bullets.title: BofA pledges $250B in US infrastructure; Goldman acquires ETF provider Neos for $2.3B
bullets.body: Bank of America announced a $250B initiative to invest in US critical infrastructure over the next year, joining Morgan Stanley ($1.5T announced earlier) and others, totaling $2.25T+ in new data-center and infrastructure investment commitments this week. Goldman Sachs separately agreed to acquire ETF provider Neos for $2.3B, expanding its passive/income product suite.
